description: A value assignment takes the current value once and ignores later input changes
code:
stock = 10
qty = 3
stock := stock - qty
qty = 5
assert(stock, 7)
stock

description: A declaration keeps following its inputs while a value assignment keeps its value
code:
price = 4
units = 3
quote = price * units
paid := price * units
price = 6
[quote, paid]

description: A value assignment replaces a standing relationship and its dependents keep updating
code:
base = 2
total = base * 10
due = total + 1
total := 5
base = 7
assert(total, 5)
due

description: An order captures the catalog price once with a value assignment in its constructor
code:
catalog = {price: 4}
class Order(qty):
    this.qty = qty
    this.price := catalog.price
first = Order(2)
catalog.price = 9
second = Order(1)
[first.price, second.price]

description: A value assignment in a conditional branch does not run again when what it read changes
code:
paid = false
stock = 10
qty = 3
if paid:
    stock := stock - qty
paid = true
assert(stock, 7)
qty = 4
stock = 20
stock

description: A value assignment records no dependency through a function call
code:
rate = 2
def fee(amount) => amount * rate
charged := fee(10)
rate = 5
assert(fee(10), 50)
charged

description: Why explains a value assignment as a stated literal
code:
a = 2
b = 3
product := a * b
step = (why product)[0]
[step.rule, step.state, step.from]

description: A value assignment cannot target a class-level property
code:
class Order
failure = ""
try:
    $Order.status := "new"
catch error:
    failure = error
failure
return: "TypeError: Cannot use ':=' on a class-level property"
